questions.explanation: Use worst or most badly. With an adverbial superlative, the may be included or omitted when natural.

questions.sentence: In the route challenge, the orange token rolled _____ than the blue token.

feedback.message: Far does not normally take a plain -er ending in standard English.
Farthest is a superlative, so it does not compare two actions with than.
The base adverb far does not make the comparison.
Both farther than and further than are accepted in this distance context.

questions.explanation: Both farther than and further than are accepted. Farther often stresses physical distance.

questions.sentence: Of the tokens in the route challenge, the orange token rolled _____.

feedback.message: Farther is comparative; this sentence needs the greatest distance.
Further is comparative; this sentence needs the greatest distance.
Do not use than with a superlative.
Both (the) farthest and (the) furthest are accepted adverbial superlatives here.

questions.explanation: Both the farthest/farthest and the furthest/furthest are accepted adverbial superlatives.
